parsed.explanation: Thin dossier: no documented trans-specific exposure of any kind — no presentation offence, no facility or custody rule, no police targeting, no violence data. The parent framework is generally protective (anti-discrimination law applying to citizens and visitors, marriage equality functioning since 2012 with one documented visitor registration), and the islands actively market themselves as welcoming. That gives no hostile signals and some positive climate, but the protections are LGB-framed and do not name gender identity; nothing documents how markers, facilities, screening or custody would actually handle a trans visitor. Per thin-data extrapolation, the structural signals (no criminalisation, working general recourse, tourism-facing welcome) resolve above elevated risk, but silence on every traveler-facing axis and the absence of documented trans-specific acceptance or enforcement keep this below the acceptance-with-protections tier: around 0.62.
